subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Tesla's Vision-Only Bet
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tesla's Vision-Only Bet usable.

hook.text: While competitors loaded their cars with lidar, Tesla stripped it all out and bet only on cameras.

buildup.text: Elon Musk argued that humans drive with eyes alone, so cameras should be enough for robots too.

discovery.text: Tesla's massive fleet sends driving data back constantly, training its neural network with billions of miles.

twist.text: Despite years of promises, Tesla's Full Self-Driving still requires a human watching the road at all times.

climax.text: The debate over cameras versus lidar remains the biggest unresolved question in autonomous driving.

punchline.text: Tesla has the most data—but not yet the most capable system.

quiz.question: What sensor does Tesla rely on exclusively for self-driving?

details.summary: Tesla controversially removed radar and ultrasonic sensors from its vehicles, betting entirely on camera-based computer vision to achieve autonomous driving, a strategy no other major AV company follows.
details.whyItMatters: If Tesla's vision-only approach succeeds, it could dramatically lower the cost of autonomous vehicles. If it fails, millions of customers own cars with potentially inferior self-driving capability.
takeaways: Tesla relies solely on eight cameras for environmental perception
Radar and ultrasonic sensors have been removed from newer models
Every other major AV developer uses multi-sensor approaches

faq.question: Why does Tesla believe cameras are sufficient?
faq.answer: Tesla argues that since humans drive using only vision, a sufficiently advanced neural network processing camera data can replicate and exceed human driving ability. The approach also dramatically reduces sensor costs.

faq.question: What are the risks of the vision-only approach?
faq.answer: Cameras can be blinded by sun glare, struggle in darkness, and cannot directly measure distance. Without redundant sensors, a camera failure or misinterpretation has no backup system to catch the error.
